body.target_estimand: Writing \(S^0_{\mathrm{target,post}}\) for the target unit's untreated potential post-period survival row, the causal target is \((S^0_{\mathrm{target,post}},\tau_R)=(S^0_{\mathrm{target,post}},q^\top\{s_1-S^0_{\mathrm{target,post}}\})\). Under exact post-transport, it is identified by the observed-law map \((\theta,\tau_R)=(yM_r^+B,q^\top\{s_1-yM_r^+B\})\).
body.estimand_functional: The observed-law estimation functional is \((\widehat\theta,\widehat\tau_R)=(\widehat y(\widehat M)_r^+\widehat B,q^\top\{\widehat s_1-\widehat y(\widehat M)_r^+\widehat B\})\), with root-\(K\) influence \((\Phi_{\theta},\Phi_\tau)\); exact post-transport supplies its causal interpretation.

sampling_model.design: A fixed set of target-pre, donor-pre, donor-post, and target factual-post cells is observed; treatment histories and grid times are fixed.
sampling_model.units: Each cell contains \(K\) independent individuals, and cell samples are mutually independent.
sampling_model.treatment: The target switches treatment after the pre period while donor units remain under control. The factual target-post event time is the treated potential time, and consistency links it to the observed event time; the untreated target-post potential time is latent. Exact post-transport, rather than a global target-pre row-space assumption, equates that untreated potential survival row with the observed-law functional \(yM_r^+B\). The Han--Shah factor embedding derives row membership from its own unit-span condition, and the rational witness derives it from invertibility of \(M\).
sampling_model.overlap: Conditional censor survival is at least \(g>0\) through every required cell horizon.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Fixed-fold cross-fitting estimates conditional event and censor survival. The positive theorem is conditional on \(a_K\to0\), \(b_K\to0\), \(a_Kb_K=o(K^{-1/2})\), a positive true and fitted event-survival tail, origin normalization, bounded variation of \(R_{cf}\), and \(\max_{c,f,\ell}\|V_{cf\ell}(X)\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(a_K)\). The last two are substantive learner restrictions, not consequences of generic machine-learning consistency. On a fixed finite support for covariates and event times, clipped empirical conditional hazard ratios and their finite product integral attain \(a_K=K^{-1/2}\); any consistent censor learner with \(b_K=o(1)\) then satisfies the product rate. This finite-stratum certificate is not asserted for generic learners or for the TCL application.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) impose event-time/censoring conditional independence given treatment and covariates, use a fixed-grid latent-factor/PCR transport, and form the spectral inputs from marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier curves; they do not derive covariate-adjusted AIPCW spectral influence inference.
Published Theorem 3 (arXiv Theorem 4) gives asymptotic linearity for a directly estimated cross-fitted doubly robust treatment-specific survival curve.

D'Alessandro, Adhikari, and Santacatterina (2026) develop covariate-adjusted outcome-regression and doubly robust survival/RMST inference for a concurrent-population platform-trial estimand, including analysis of pooling non-concurrent controls.
Theorem 2 and Corollary 2 give row-space out-of-sample prediction guarantees for minimum-norm principal component regression.
Equation (4.12) gives the Fr\'echet derivative of the Moore--Penrose inverse under locally constant rank.
Sections 3--4 show interpolation, variance, and survival-curve bias for synthetic survival individuals.
Theorem 3.1 gives feasible inference for low-rank linear functionals when the working rank overestimates the true rank.

Theorem 2.1 recovers the factor space for bounded working rank at least the true rank as the cross-sectional dimension grows, and Theorem 3.2 with Corollary 3.1 gives over-estimated-rank-robust factor-augmented inference.

body.tldr: For fixed donor count, pre grid, post grid, and exact rank of the fixed donor-pre matrix, the required positive rank-\(r\) separation follows from \(\sigma_r(M)>0=\sigma_{r+1}(M)\); no additional singular-gap assumption is imposed. Covariate-adjusted cross-fitted AIPCW cell estimates have a joint root-\(K\) expansion conditional on a positive true and fitted event-survival tail and explicit bounded-variation and relative-variation restrictions for the selected event learner. A clipped empirical hazard learner satisfies those restrictions with \(a_K=K^{-1/2}\) on a fixed finite-stratum submodel, but this certificate is not a generic learner result and does not verify the TCL application. Exact post-transport, without a global target-pre row-space assumption, identifies the untreated potential curve with the observed-law spectral representation. The full three-block spectral derivative yields a possibly singular joint Gaussian law; positive coordinate variances suffice for the simultaneous band and a positive grid-RMST variance suffices for scalar studentization. A full-data causal construction, preserving all six observed margins, proves that unadjusted Kaplan--Meier/PCR has fixed bias on a relatively open subclass. Weak-gap and selected-rank inference remains open.

project_justification.gap: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) already state event-time/censoring conditional independence given treatment and covariates, but their spectral workflow uses marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier curves and does not give a covariate-adjusted joint influence law. With heterogeneous covariates, conditional independence need not imply marginal independence, so those cell inputs can converge to distorted curves before PCR transport. Westling et al. (2024, published Theorem 3 (arXiv Theorem 4)) provide asymptotic-linearity theory for a directly estimated treatment-specific curve, not for a learned three-block spectral counterfactual.
project_justification.niche: With \(N_0,T_0,J,r\) fixed and \(K\to\infty\), covariate-standardized cell curves form a finite-dimensional semiparametric first stage. Exact rank of the fixed donor-pre matrix itself gives \(\sigma_r(M)>0=\sigma_{r+1}(M)\), so the counterfactual is a smooth local spectral functional without a separate singular-gap assumption. The bridge requires a positive event-survival tail that defines the score, the exact Stieltjes remainder under a disclosed learner-path variation restriction, a concrete submodel on which that restriction is attainable, and all three terms of the pseudoinverse derivative.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the conditional-learner AIPCW cell expansion, a finite-stratum clipped-hazard attainability certificate, the joint transported Gaussian law with possibly singular covariance, a Gaussian-multiplier band under positive coordinate variances, and a studentized grid-RMST interval under positive variance for the declared scalar contrast. It also constructs a full-data potential-outcome witness, with unchanged observed margins and verified exact transport, that places unadjusted Kaplan--Meier/PCR bias on a relatively open causal subclass. Weak-gap inference remains open.

body.related_work: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) supply the fixed-grid latent-factor survival panel, unit and time spans, PCR transport, and the 925-patient, 10-country TCL application. They assume event-time/censoring conditional independence given treatment and covariates, but use marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier inputs and do not derive a covariate-adjusted transported influence law. Proposition~\ref{prop:han-shah-fixed-grid-embedding} gives their algebraic span bridge, while the joint limit itself needs exact post-transport but no global target-pre row-space assumption. Proposition~\ref{prop:km-pcr-cancellation} now supplies a full-data potential-outcome witness: its latent untreated target-post time verifies transport while its treated factual time preserves the observed target-post margin, and continuous attachment yields a relatively open causal biased subclass. Westling, Luedtke, Gilbert, and Carone (2024, published Theorem 3 (arXiv Theorem 4) and Sections 5.2--5.3) supply direct-curve cross-fitted augmented survival inference. D'Alessandro, Adhikari, and Santacatterina (2026, arXiv:2603.10989) study covariate-adjusted DR survival and RMST inference for the concurrent-population platform-trial estimand while assessing whether shared non-concurrent controls may be pooled; that direct shared-control influence function is distinct from the learned fixed-panel three-block spectral transport here. The relative-survival variation restriction here is an additional primitive sufficient condition not imposed by Westling et al., who instead assume the exact Stieltjes-remainder rate. Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-stratum-hazard-certificate} proves that restriction for a fixed finite-stratum clipped empirical hazard learner, not for generic learners. Agarwal, Shah, and Shen (2025, Theorem 2 and Corollary 2) study minimum-norm PCR and row-space prediction without censoring-aware asymptotics. Golub and Pereyra (1973, equation (4.12)) provide the constant-rank pseudoinverse differential. Curth, Poon, Nori, and Gonz\'alez (2024, Sections 3--4) analyze survival synthetic-control bias but not this three-block PCR pseudo-limit or its full-data causal open subclass. Fan and Liao (2022) study growing-panel factor models, and Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2026) study robustness to rank misspecification. These are neighboring problems; weak-gap and selected-rank inference for the unregularized fixed-donor target remains an acknowledged open frontier of this note.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The positive theory is fixed-dimensional and conditional on a positive true and fitted event-survival tail and an event learner whose relative-survival path has the stated bounded variation and \(L_2\) variation rate. Ordinary supremum or \(L_2\) consistency does not imply that property. The finite-stratum hazard certificate establishes attainability only for fixed covariate and event-time supports with uniformly positive at-risk probabilities, event hazards bounded away from one, and proportional training samples; it does not verify the restriction for generic learners or for the TCL data. For the fixed matrix \(M\), exact rank already supplies the positive local rank-\(r\) separation used in differentiation, so there is no standalone singular-gap restriction. This argument is not uniform over triangular arrays with \(\sigma_r(M_K)\to0\). The joint Gaussian covariance may be singular, but the band excludes zero counterfactual coordinate variances and the grid-RMST interval excludes zero variance in its scalar direction. The theory does not cover growing grids or panels, selected rank, approximate post-transport, or continuous-time RMST.
body.honest_scope: The joint cell expansion is a conditional-learner theorem under within-cell i.i.d. sampling, cross-cell independence for stacking, conditional independent censoring, censor positivity, fixed-fold nuisance consistency and product rate, a positive true and fitted event-survival tail, origin normalization, and explicit bounded-variation and relative-variation restrictions. A concrete clipped empirical hazard learner discharges the event-side restrictions with root-\(K\) rate only on the stated fixed finite-stratum submodel; this does not establish generic learner attainability or verify the 925-patient TCL application. The spectral limit additionally requires fixed panel dimensions, exact rank of the fixed donor-pre matrix, and exact post-transport, which is its sole global causal-identification equality. Exact rank implies the fixed positive separation \(\sigma_r(M)>0=\sigma_{r+1}(M)\), so no separate singular-gap assumption is required; the result is not uniform for a sequence of matrices with a closing gap. No global target-pre row-space assumption is imposed: the Han--Shah embedding derives row membership from its own factor-span hypotheses, and the full-data rational witness derives it from invertibility. The witness explicitly separates treated and untreated target-post potential times, imposes consistency, preserves all six observed margins, and proves a relatively open causal subclass with fixed Kaplan--Meier/PCR bias. The joint covariance may be singular. The simultaneous band requires positive counterfactual marginal variances, and the studentized grid-RMST interval separately requires positive variance of \(q^\top(\Phi_1-\Phi_\theta)\). Applying either conclusion to TCL requires independent verification of all sampling, learner, transport, and relevant variance conditions. Nothing here covers growing dimensions, selected rank, approximate transport, or continuous-time RMST. Weak-gap inference remains the acknowledged follow-on question because its frontier also depends on weak loadings and a uniform triangular experiment, not only on \(\sigma_r(M_K)\).
